title: Conservative cohort ramp with synthetic-control groups for pinned model promotions
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: We need a low-risk promotion pattern for pinned model revisions that combines conservative cohort ramps with synthetic control groups (mirror holdouts) and automatic rollback gates. This ticket defines the product-level policy, success criteria, and instrumentation required so engineering can implement the gating and console UX.

Motivation: Customers who pin a model version expect predictable latency and quality after a revision swap. Existing canary patterns expose customers to either too much traffic early (risking quality/regression) or too little signal (delaying rollouts). The proposed approach reduces blast radius while producing statistically useful signals faster by using holdout/synthetic controls, progressive cohort ramps, and multi-signal gates (latency, cost, quality, safety).

Goals:
- Define a default pinned-promotion workflow that is conservative by default but configurable per-customer.
- Publish the performance profile and rollout requirements to the model catalog when onboarding new model revisions.
- Ensure rollouts surface both operational (latency/error) and qualitative (prompt-level evals, rerank metrics) signals for decisioning.

Out of scope: full automatic rollback enforcement for Dedicated capacity (infrastructure changes will be separate), UX redesign of the pin management page (small console additions only).
acceptance_criteria: Product policy doc describing default ramp schedule, control group size, and gate thresholds exists in Confluence and is linked from the model catalog
Telemetry hooks are defined for the set of signals (latency p50/p95, token-rate change, error rate, generation quality scores, hallucination heuristics) and a sample dashboard mock is available
A minimal console flow to start a pinned promotion with: (1) choose cohorts, (2) schedule ramps, (3) enable synthetic control, and (4) choose fallback variant is spec'd
On-call and runbook steps for investigating gating failures are drafted and reviewed by SRE
Documentation for customers on how to opt into an aggressive ramp profile or use holdout-only validation is published
success_metrics: Median rollback rate for pinned promotions <= 3% after GA compared to current baseline
Time-to-detect quality regressions (A/B signal) reduced by 25% through synthetic controls
Number of customer-reported regressions after pin swaps reduced by 40% within first 90 days
Adoption: 30% of pinned promotions initiated through console use the conservative ramp within first quarter
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal shadow validation (mirror traffic) against existing pinned variant for 48 hours. Phase 1: Small holdout cohort (1% traffic) + synthetic control group for 72 hours with tight latency and error gates. Phase 2: Progressive ramp to 5%/15%/35% over 24/48/72 hours conditional on gate pass. Phase 3: Promote to full traffic with adjustable surge buffer and rollback policy. Default ramp uses conservative thresholds; customers can select 'accelerated' profile. All ramps publish performance profile to the model catalog on completion.
monitoring_playbook: Primary runbook: verify telemetry ingestion, check p95 latency and error rate, inspect quality eval sample, and compare to synthetic-control baseline. If any gate trips, reduce traffic to previous safe step and trigger on-call. Post-rollback checklist: collect sample prompts, run targeted evals, open incident with 'Pinned Model Regression' template, notify customer if customer-facing. Links to playbooks in Confluence included in links field.
qa_plan: Preflight: run end-to-end simulation using replayed traffic and the new model revision in mirror mode. Smoke tests: latency and correctness checks on canonical prompt set. A/B validation: run paired-sample tests on internal holdout cohorts. Post-merge: maintain daily quality checks for first 7 days after promotion. QA sign-off required before Phase 1 begins.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Aisha Kumar: Initial draft created. Shared with eng and SRE for feasibility. Asked ENG to estimate effort and identify infra gaps.
2025-02-25 - Priya Nandakumar (ENG): Core runtime can support mirror traffic but we need a small routing flag for prefix-based cohorting; ENG-37421 opened to address routing change.
2025-02-28 - SRE (Jorge Martinez): Requested clear failure thresholds for p95 and error rate. Proposed default rollback at p95 > baseline + 120ms sustained 5m or error_rate > 0.5% absolute increase.
2025-03-03 - Design (Mina Park): Console mock uploaded, suggests an explicit 'synthetic control' toggle and a visual diff for key telemetry. Linking PRD and mock in links.

2025-03-06 - Liam O'Connor: Updated rollout plan to include 48h internal shadow validation step per ENG feedback. Assigned ENG-38099 for telemetry schema changes. Marking security review required for publishing performance profiles to model catalog.
notes: Trade-offs: conservative default reduces speed of promotions but lowers customer risk. Offering an accelerated profile keeps flexibility for low-risk customers.
Decision: synthetic control groups are preferred to pure canaries for faster statistical power on quality metrics without increasing customer-facing variance.
Follow-ups: add a small ML-eval pipeline job to compute paired-sample significance for A/B quality signals (tracked in ENG backlog).
